items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: I never did really talk to Condon more in just a few maybe remarks here and there in my life

ctx.x: Yeah, Louie and Oliver and Bessie Smith just everybody that I sort of liked and including some of the Boogie Woogie pianists. Medlux Lewis was already in New York at that time came there in the fall of 38. No, that's right Medlux hadn't gotten to New York when it started on Jazzman. But I'd written an article on Boogie Woogie for Panacea's magazine which had come out oh, several months before we started on Jazzman and Ramsey had read that and liked the article so that's why he asked me to write an article on…

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-08-31
items.q: I don't mean Eddie Conlon, he's a very good talker and quite a friendly guy

ctx.x: You want to talk about some of these musicians you've encountered in the course of your career now?

Yes, I might talk a little bit. I happened to pick up an old big box at home I have called Notes, and I dug out a few of the notebooks and other things. One package of notes envelope called Jazzmen material that we collected in 1938 when we were working on Jazzmen. Unfortunately then, we not only didn't have tape recording, we didn't have any other recorders. Nobody was hardly recording interviews.
